waypoints.name: Heliotrope Ridge Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542), continue about 1 mile east of the Glacier Public Service Center and turn right onto Glacier Creek Road (FS 39). Drive about 8 miles, turn left at a junction and continue less than half a mile to the Heliotrope Ridge Trailhead for Trail 677, at about 3,700 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: Hogsback Camp
waypoints.directions: Follow Trail 677 through old growth, crossing Grouse, Kulshan and Heliotrope Creeks (lowest early in the day), to the signed fork at about 2.25 miles. Go right on the climbers' path up the crest of the Hogsback moraine to the camps around 6,000 ft at the edge of the Coleman Glacier.

waypoints.name: North Ridge Base / Coleman Glacier Junction
waypoints.directions: Rope up and cross the Coleman Glacier east (climber's left) toward the toe of the North Ridge, threading seracs and open crevasses; the route changes yearly and often has no track. Arrive at the double bergschrund guarding the base of the ridge, and probe as you near it for a hidden third crack between the two visible ones.

waypoints.name: Mount Baker Summit
waypoints.directions: Cross the double bergschrund on a bridge or narrow ramp and climb the broad 40 degree snow gully to the ridge crest. Follow the crest to the ice cliff near 9,600 ft and climb its steep ice, short near-vertical steps then sustained 60 to 65 degree ice, for several pitches. Above it the angle eases; trend climber's left through crevasses on the upper ice cap to the summit plateau and Grant Peak.

The 'North Ridge Base / Coleman Glacier Junction' pin sits on a moving glacier near the bergschrund - an approximate base only; it cannot be locked. Baker Highway (SR 542) below Glacier is open; only the Artist Point section closed 25 Oct 2026.

waypoints.name: Shannon Ridge Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Drive Baker Lake Road (Forest Road 11) north from SR 20 near milepost 82, then turn onto FR 1152 and follow the 1152-014 spur to its end at about 2,500 feet, where the trail begins. The spur is rough and rutted, so high clearance is the sensible minimum for the drive in. If you're staying overnight in the park, you'll need a North Cascades backcountry permit, obtained in person at Marblemount or arranged with the wilderness office ahead of time.

waypoints.name: Timberline Junction
waypoints.directions: Follow Shannon Ridge Trail #742, an old roadbed heading northeast, for about 2 miles to where the road tread ends near 3,800 ft, weaving through a belt of blowdown. Continue on true trail angling left through brush onto the open ridge crest and up to timberline near 4,600 ft, where snow often lingers into midsummer.

waypoints.name: Shannon Ridge / Sulphide Glacier Camp
waypoints.directions: From timberline, follow the broad, rolling crest of Shannon Ridge through meadows and broken timber for about 2 miles to a pass near 5,400 ft, where a north-south ridge is met and the Sulphide Glacier and summit pyramid first come into view. Continue up open slopes and snow onto the toe of the glacier to the lower camp at about 6,200 ft; an upper camp sits near 6,500 ft. There is no reliable water late in the season.

waypoints.name: Mount Shuksan Summit Pyramid
waypoints.directions: Rope up at camp and climb northward, keeping to the western edge of the Sulphide Glacier over a series of rolling steps; near 7,600 ft the angle eases, so bear north-northeast across the upper glacier to the foot of the summit pyramid at about 8,400-8,500 ft. Cross the moat and climb the central gully on the pyramid's south face, the one with rappel anchors, roughly 600 ft of steep snow or blocky rock to the summit.

waypoints.name: Bedal Creek / Bedal Basin Trailhead (end of FR 4096)
waypoints.directions: Drive the Mountain Loop Highway to Forest Road 4096 and follow that rough, narrow spur - a 4WD road about three miles long where high clearance genuinely helps - to its end at the Bedal Creek trailhead, around 2,790 feet.

waypoints.name: Climber's trail turnoff on Bedal Creek Trail
waypoints.directions: Walk the old Bedal Creek Trail about 1.5 miles and 700 ft to around 3,500 ft, where a climbers' path, often marked with pink flagging, turns off to the left. Watch for it: the old tread continues and dies in a brushy washout below the basin.

waypoints.name: Sloan Peak Summit
waypoints.directions: Climb the path steeply through forest to talus near 4,900 ft, then bend southeast to the Bedal-Sloan saddle at 5,300 ft. Continue southeast over a rock ridge near 5,800 ft, rope up and cross the Sloan Glacier southwest to the rock near 7,100 ft. Follow the exposed heather shelf of the Corkscrew across the south face onto the west face, climb the gully to the crest, then a short class 4 step and third class to the summit.

road.name: Bedal Creek Trailhead (FR-4096), off Mountain Loop Highway
road.status: Closed for the winter. The Forest Service shut the Mountain Loop Highway from Bedal Campground south to Barlow Pass on 16 November 2026, and the FR 4096 turnoff lies inside that stretch; it sets the reopening date each spring. Walking, snowshoeing and skiing stay allowed.
road.driveNote: Roughly 1.5-2 hours from Seattle via US-2/SR-92/Mountain Loop Highway to the Bedal Creek Trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: FR roads off the Mountain Loop Highway are typically only reliably open late spring through fall; check Darrington Ranger District/USFS alerts for current status.

waypoints.name: Sunrise Mine Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east about 27 to 28 miles, then turn onto Sunrise Mine Road, Forest Road 4065. Follow roughly 2.3 to 2.5 miles of gravel to the road's end at the Sunrise Mine Trailhead, where Trail No. 707 starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

waypoints.name: Vesper Peak
waypoints.directions: Take Trail 707 across the unbridged South Fork Stillaguamish and up through forest and a talus basin to the steep, loose couloir and Headlee Pass, about 2.7 miles in. Traverse below Sperry Peak into the upper Vesper Creek basin, leave the lake trail at the creek crossing, and climb the steep bootpath to treeline, then about 1,000 ft of granite slabs on the central rib, following cairns, to the summit.
